chapters.title: What Is Science?
chapters.tease: A method for finding out which ideas survive contact with reality, and for catching our own mistakes.

chapters.title: Observation and Measurement
chapters.tease: Observation tells you something happened; measurement tells you how much, and how sure you can be.

chapters.title: The Experiment
chapters.tease: Change one thing, hold the rest steady, compare: the simple trick behind every drug, vaccine and bridge.

chapters.title: Hypotheses and Theories
chapters.tease: A hypothesis is a guess you can test; a theory is a framework that has survived every test so far.

chapters.title: Models and Simulations
chapters.tease: A model strips the world down to what matters; a simulation sets it running to see what follows.

chapters.title: Instruments That Changed Science
chapters.tease: Every instrument extends a sense, then shows something no sense had suspected.

chapters.title: Error, Uncertainty and Statistics
chapters.tease: An honest result is a number with a range attached; doubt, properly measured, is science's currency.

chapters.title: Peer Review and Replication
chapters.tease: A result becomes science when strangers have examined it, tried to break it, and failed.

chapters.title: Scientific Revolutions
chapters.tease: A field's deepest assumptions are invisible until they break, and then everything looks different.

chapters.title: What Science Cannot Tell Us
chapters.tease: Science tells us what is; it cannot tell us what ought to be, and knowing the boundary is a strength.

chapters.title: From Four Elements to Atoms
chapters.tease: The slow move from four philosophical elements to atoms you can weigh, and finally see.

chapters.title: Dalton's Atoms
chapters.tease: Dalton turned atoms from a philosophy into a bookkeeping system a chemist could check on a balance.

chapters.title: Mendeleev's Table
chapters.tease: A chart with holes in it, filled by three new elements, and the proof that chemistry has an order.

chapters.title: Discovering the Electron
chapters.tease: A glowing beam in a glass tube revealed that atoms have parts, and that electricity comes in lumps.

chapters.title: Rutherford's Nucleus
chapters.tease: A student's tedious counting job revealed that the atom is almost entirely empty space around a tiny nucleus.

chapters.title: Protons and Neutrons
chapters.tease: The neutron hid in plain sight for two years because it carried no charge; Chadwick found it in a fortnight.

chapters.title: Isotopes
chapters.tease: Atoms of one element come in several weights, and the differences are clocks, thermometers and tracers.

chapters.title: Radioactivity
chapters.tease: Atoms that fall apart on their own, found by a fogged photographic plate, opened the door to the nucleus.

chapters.title: Making New Elements
chapters.tease: Beyond uranium every element is human-made, a few atoms at a time, by four rival laboratories.

chapters.title: Inside the Proton: Quarks
chapters.tease: The proton has parts, found the same way the nucleus was, and its mass is almost entirely energy.

chapters.title: Chemical Bonds
chapters.tease: Every material, medicine and molecule exists because atoms share, trade or pool their outer electrons.

chapters.title: Reactions and Equations
chapters.tease: Atoms are never created or destroyed in a reaction, only rearranged: the first exact law of chemistry.

chapters.title: Acids and Bases
chapters.tease: One brewer's logarithm turned a taste test into a number that governs blood, soil, oceans and beer.

chapters.title: Catalysts and Enzymes
chapters.tease: By lowering the energy hill, catalysts make the impossible routine, from fertiliser to the enzymes keeping you alive.

chapters.title: Combustion and Fire
chapters.tease: Fire was a mystery for 100,000 years; a balance, a gas and a candle turned it into chemistry.

chapters.title: Electrochemistry and Batteries
chapters.tease: From a twitching frog to the cell in your pocket, batteries turn a held-apart reaction into current.

chapters.title: Carbon: the Chemistry of Life
chapters.tease: Four bonds and a taste for itself make carbon the backbone of life, fuel, plastics and the diamond trade.

chapters.title: Plastics and Polymers
chapters.tease: Giant molecules made to order gave the twentieth century its materials and the twenty-first its waste problem.

chapters.title: Fertilisers and the Haber Process
chapters.tease: Breaking nitrogen's triple bond in a steel reactor feeds about half the people on Earth.

chapters.title: Green Chemistry
chapters.tease: Counting the atoms that end up as waste turned chemistry from a yield game into a design discipline.

chapters.title: Galileo's Falling Bodies
chapters.tease: By slowing gravity down a ramp, Galileo showed that all bodies fall alike and distance grows as time squared.

chapters.title: Newton's Three Laws
chapters.tease: Three sentences published in 1687 still describe every push, pull, crash, launch and orbit in the ordinary world.

chapters.title: Universal Gravitation
chapters.tease: One law joined the falling apple to the Moon, predicted a comet and a planet, and let a shy chemist weigh the Earth.

chapters.title: Friction
chapters.tease: The force that stops a car and warms your hands is a landscape of microscopic peaks welding and tearing apart.

chapters.title: Pressure and Fluids
chapters.tease: A tube of mercury proved the air has weight, and a century of experiments turned pressure into engineering.

chapters.title: Buoyancy and Flight
chapters.tease: A fluid pushes harder from below than above; that one imbalance floats ships, lifts balloons and flies aeroplanes.

chapters.title: Momentum and Collisions
chapters.tease: Mass times velocity is never created or destroyed; the rule governs crashes, rockets and the invention of the neutrino.

chapters.title: Circular Motion and Orbits
chapters.tease: An orbit is a fall that keeps missing: fire a cannonball fast enough and the ground curves away beneath it for ever.

chapters.title: Levers, Pulleys and Gears
chapters.tease: Simple machines trade distance for force; they built the pyramids, the cathedrals and the gearbox in every car.

chapters.title: Chaos and the Limits of Prediction
chapters.tease: A rounding error in a 1961 weather model showed that determined does not mean predictable.

chapters.title: What Is Energy?
chapters.tease: A single bookkeeping quantity that pays for every change in the universe, from toast to lightning.

chapters.title: Conservation of Energy
chapters.tease: Heat and work were shown to be the same currency, and the total never changes, however hard you shake it.

chapters.title: Heat and Temperature
chapters.tease: The thermometer made temperature a number, and a cannon borer showed heat was motion, not a fluid.

chapters.title: Engines and Thermodynamics
chapters.tease: A 28-year-old engineer worked out the maximum efficiency of every engine that would ever be built.

chapters.title: Entropy and the Arrow of Time
chapters.tease: The only law of physics with a built-in direction: disorder wins because it has more ways to happen.

chapters.title: What Is Light?
chapters.tease: Nine centuries of argument over whether light is particle or wave, settled by two slits, a shadow and a sheet of metal.

chapters.title: Colour and the Spectrum
chapters.tease: A beam through a shutter showed white light is a mixture, and the gaps in it tell us what stars are made of.

chapters.title: Lenses, Mirrors and Telescopes
chapters.tease: Two Dutch lenses in a tube became Galileo's window on Jupiter and the ancestor of a 39-metre mirror in Chile.

chapters.title: Lasers
chapters.tease: A ruby rod and a flashbulb produced light in which every wave marches in step, and it now runs the internet.

chapters.title: Energy for a Warming World
chapters.tease: Sixty years after a Bell Labs silicon cell, the carbon cost of a kilowatt-hour decides the century.

chapters.title: Static Electricity
chapters.tease: Amber and fur became a stored charge in a jar, then a tamed lightning bolt, in one astonishing century.

chapters.title: Current, Voltage and Resistance
chapters.tease: A stack of coins and brine gave the world steady current, and a schoolteacher found the law it obeys.

chapters.title: Magnets and the Earth's Field
chapters.tease: A carved lodestone sphere showed the planet is a magnet; its molten core is the dynamo that keeps it so.

chapters.title: Electromagnetism
chapters.tease: A twitching needle showed that moving charge makes magnetism, and gave the world the motor and the telegraph.

chapters.title: Faraday's Dynamo
chapters.tease: Move a conductor through a magnetic field and current flows: every power station since is this experiment.

chapters.title: Maxwell's Equations
chapters.tease: One added term joined electricity, magnetism and light, and every radio and phone since obeys the result.

chapters.title: The Electromagnetic Spectrum
chapters.tease: A thermometer laid beyond the red end of a rainbow began the discovery of fifty invisible octaves of light.

chapters.title: Sound Waves
chapters.tease: Pressure ripples through matter at 343 metres a second, a figure found with cannons, and read today by sonar and scans.

chapters.title: Semiconductors and the Transistor
chapters.tease: A three-man experiment with gold foil and germanium gave the world the switch on which everything now runs.

chapters.title: Superconductors
chapters.tease: Cool mercury to four degrees above absolute zero and its resistance vanishes, a quantum effect you can hold.

chapters.title: The Speed of Light
chapters.tease: Once light had a speed, the universe had a clock, a ruler and a speed limit all in one number.

chapters.title: Special Relativity
chapters.tease: If light's speed is the same for everyone, then time and length cannot be; Einstein followed that logic to the end.

chapters.title: E = mc²
chapters.tease: Mass is energy in a very tight package; the exchange rate, c squared, is why the Sun burns and why atoms can be split.

chapters.title: General Relativity
chapters.tease: Gravity is not a pull but a curve in spacetime; a solar eclipse in 1919 showed the starlight bending as predicted.

chapters.title: Gravitational Waves
chapters.tease: A ripple a thousandth of a proton wide, caught by two L-shaped instruments: astronomy gained hearing.

chapters.title: The Quantum Leap
chapters.tease: Energy comes in packets; a quantum leap is the smallest change nature allows, and it lights every neon sign and laser.

chapters.title: Wave-Particle Duality
chapters.tease: Electrons interfere like waves and land like particles; which face they show depends on the question you ask.

chapters.title: Uncertainty and Probability
chapters.tease: Nature keeps a book of odds: the quantum wave gives probabilities, and position and momentum can never both be sharp.

chapters.title: Entanglement
chapters.tease: Einstein called it spooky action at a distance; fifty years of Bell tests proved the spookiness real.

chapters.title: The Standard Model
chapters.tease: Seventeen particles and three forces explain every laboratory result for fifty years; the gaps are the next frontier.

chapters.title: Deep Time
chapters.tease: Rocks are clocks: once uranium's decay could be read, the Earth's age went from a guess to 4.54 billion years.

chapters.title: Fossils and the Rock Record
chapters.tease: Steno's three rules turned cliffs into calendars; Smith, Anning and Cuvier filled the pages with vanished creatures.

chapters.title: Continental Drift to Plate Tectonics
chapters.tease: The continents really do move; it took sonar, magnetism and a rift down the middle of the Atlantic to prove it.

chapters.title: Seismology: Listening to the Earth
chapters.tease: Earthquakes ring the planet like a bell; reading the echoes revealed a liquid outer core and a solid heart.

chapters.title: The Atmosphere
chapters.tease: Ten tonnes of air stand on every square metre; barometers, balloons and one honest instrument mapped it.

chapters.title: Ocean Currents
chapters.tease: The oceans are a thousand-year conveyor belt of heat, salt and carbon, first charted for the sake of the mail.

chapters.title: Ice Ages
chapters.tease: Ice once buried Canada three kilometres deep; wobbles of Earth's orbit, read from mud and ice, explain why.

chapters.title: The Greenhouse Effect
chapters.tease: A few gases keep Earth 33 degrees warmer than bare rock; Foote, Tyndall and Arrhenius showed which, and why.

chapters.title: Measuring Climate Change
chapters.tease: Thousands of instruments and five independent teams agree: 1.1 degrees of warming, and a fossil-carbon fingerprint.

chapters.title: Earth from Space
chapters.tease: Once we could look back at the planet, its weather, ice and forests became measurable, and so did we.

chapters.title: The Microscope Reveals Cells
chapters.tease: A ground glass bead showed that every living thing is built from cells, and that every cell comes from a cell.

chapters.title: Germs and Microbiology
chapters.tease: Specific microbes cause specific diseases: the idea that gave us hand-washing, vaccines, antiseptics and antibiotics.

chapters.title: Photosynthesis
chapters.tease: Plants split water with sunlight and build sugar from air: the reaction behind every meal and every breath.

chapters.title: Darwin and Natural Selection
chapters.tease: Variation plus inheritance plus scarcity equals design without a designer: the idea that explains all of life.

chapters.title: Mendel's Peas
chapters.tease: Inheritance comes in particles, not blends: a friar's 28,000 pea plants gave biology its first mathematical law.

chapters.title: The Double Helix
chapters.tease: A twisted ladder with matching rungs explains how life copies itself; the photograph that revealed it has its own story.

chapters.title: How Genes Make Proteins
chapters.tease: Four letters, read three at a time, build every protein alive: the same code in bacteria and in you.

chapters.title: Genome Sequencing
chapters.tease: Reading three billion letters went from a fifteen-year, three-billion-dollar project to a day's work on a desktop.

chapters.title: Editing Genes: CRISPR
chapters.tease: A yoghurt bacterium's immune memory became a tool that rewrites genes to order, and the first cure arrived in 2023.

chapters.title: The Origin of Life
chapters.tease: Sparks in a flask made the building blocks of life in a week; vents, meteorites and RNA now suggest how they assembled.

chapters.title: The Copernican Revolution
chapters.tease: Moving the Earth out of the centre took 1,400 years of argument and three centuries of proof.

chapters.title: Kepler's Laws
chapters.tease: Eight arcminutes of error that Kepler refused to ignore turned circles into ellipses and astronomy into physics.

chapters.title: How Stars Shine
chapters.tease: The Sun loses four million tonnes a second as light: fusion, not fire, and it took neutrinos to prove it.

chapters.title: Life and Death of Stars
chapters.tease: Stars are born, burn and die by a schedule set by their mass, and their deaths made the atoms you are built from.

chapters.title: Measuring the Universe
chapters.tease: Every cosmic distance rests on a chain of calibrations that starts with one star shifting by a third of an arcsecond.

chapters.title: Hubble and the Expanding Universe
chapters.tease: Faint smudges of light, all red-shifted, revealed that space itself is stretching and had a beginning.

chapters.title: The Cosmic Microwave Background
chapters.tease: A hiss that would not go away turned out to be the afterglow of the Big Bang, still filling every corner of space.

chapters.title: Dark Matter
chapters.tease: Galaxies spin too fast for the matter we can see; five sixths of the universe's matter is something unknown.

chapters.title: Dark Energy
chapters.tease: Distant supernovae were too faint: the expansion is speeding up, and 68 per cent of the universe is something unknown.

chapters.title: Are We Alone?
chapters.tease: Thousands of planets, billions of habitable worlds, and still only one biology: the question the book ends on.
